title: Banking & Financial Services
tagline: Tellers, personal bankers, loan officers, and analysts — careers inside the financial system.
summary: Banking careers span retail branches, lending, credit analysis, and compliance — licensed or credential-light entry points that grow into well-paid lending, wealth, and risk roles. This roadmap covers the branch ladder, the NMLS lending path, credit analysis, and the compliance backbone.

detail.description: Banking spans retail branches (accounts, loans, service), commercial lending, wealth management, operations, and risk/compliance — with careers that start customer-facing and grow analytical.
detail.why: Banks hire steadily in every city, train extensively, and promote from within — the branch is one of the last true apprenticeship floors in finance.
learn: Read the BLS OOH loan officers profile
Compare retail bank vs credit union vs commercial bank employers
Map the roles inside one branch
Identify which lane attracts you: service, lending, or analysis
tasks: Evaluate, authorize, or recommend approval of commercial, real estate, or credit loans; advise borrowers on financial status and payment methods.

detail.description: The ladder: teller → personal banker → assistant branch manager → branch manager; lateral tracks: loan officer, credit analyst, compliance officer, operations.
detail.why: Banking promotes from within — knowing the map helps you sequence roles deliberately instead of waiting to be chosen.
learn: List the roles in a branch and their responsibilities
Note which roles require licenses (NMLS) vs internal training
Compare bank vs credit union cultures
Set a 5-year target role

detail.description: Working fluency in deposits and lending: how banks earn (spread), credit scores and reports, loan structures, interest math, and the basic regulatory duty of care.
detail.why: Every banking role translates money concepts for customers — fluency is the product.
learn: Explain how a bank earns money on deposits
Read a credit report end-to-end
Master simple/compound interest and amortization math
Learn the 5 Cs of credit (character, capacity, capital, collateral, conditions)

resources.title: Khan Academy — Finance and capital markets

detail.description: Banks operate under intense regulation (KYC, BSA/AML, fair lending) — accuracy, discretion, and doing things by the book are the professional baseline.
detail.why: Compliance awareness from day one is what banks screen for; shortcuts end careers in this industry.
learn: Learn what KYC (know your customer) means
Understand BSA/AML purpose at a high level
Practice strict accuracy in every mock transaction
Study fair-lending principles briefly

detail.description: The classic entry: processing transactions accurately, cash drawers that balance, identifying customer needs, and referrals to bankers — speed plus zero errors.
detail.why: Teller work teaches the bank's products, systems, and customers — and is the standard first rung for branch careers.
learn: Practice cash handling to zero-variance standard
Learn core transactions: deposits, withdrawals, transfers, holds
Master your bank's systems and overrides politely
Log daily referral conversations
tasks: Receive and pay out money; keep records of money and negotiable instruments involved in a financial institution's various transactions.

detail.description: Personal bankers open accounts, recommend products, handle service issues, and originate small loans — the relationship role where sales skill and care meet.
detail.why: This is where branch careers accelerate: goal-carrying bankers who balance sales with genuine care get promoted fastest.
learn: Learn the consumer product suite deeply
Practice needs-based conversations (not product-pushing)
Understand account opening and KYC steps
Track referral and goal metrics weekly

detail.description: Customer due diligence: identity verification, beneficial-ownership questions for businesses, CIP requirements, and spotting red flags that need escalation.
detail.why: Onboarding is where compliance meets the customer — doing it well is a real, promotable skill.
learn: Learn CIP (Customer Identification Program) elements
Practice document verification standards
Know the red flags that trigger escalation
Keep clean, complete files every time

detail.description: The catalog: checking/savings, CDs, money markets, credit cards, personal loans, auto, mortgages, HELOCs, and small-business products — with the fees and rules of each.
detail.why: Advisors who know every product's real use case can match needs honestly — and win referrals for it.
learn: Build a one-page summary per product family
Compare similar products across two banks
Learn common fee structures and waivers
Practice matching needs to products

detail.description: Operations runs the machinery: payment processing, fraud monitoring, item handling, reconciliations, and service teams — steady, detail-focused careers away from sales goals.
detail.why: Ops is the no-sales alternative lane — ideal for meticulous people, and a quiet path into fraud and compliance roles.
learn: Explore operations job postings at local banks
Learn payment rails basics (ACH, wires, cards)
Practice reconciliation exercises
Note the fraud-analyst career branch

resources.title: BLS OOH — Business and Financial occupations

detail.description: Loan officers evaluate applications, explain products, structure deals, and shepherd approvals — in consumer, mortgage, or commercial flavors, often with production incentives.
detail.why: Lending is banking's highest-paid branch lane and the natural destination for strong bankers.
learn: Learn the loan lifecycle: application → underwriting → closing
Practice reading credit files and debt ratios
Shadow a loan officer for a day
Ask about your bank's internal LO development

detail.description: Mortgage loan originators must be licensed through NMLS: pre-licensing education (20 hours), a national test, background/credit checks, and annual renewals with CE.
detail.why: The NMLS license is the legal key to residential mortgage origination — many banks sponsor strong employees through it.
learn: Review NMLS pre-licensing and test requirements
Ask your employer about sponsorship
Complete 20 hours of approved education
Pass the SAFE MLO national test

certs.name: MLO License (NMLS)
certs.issuer: State regulators via the Nationwide Multistate Licensing System
certs.note: 20 hours of pre-licensing education, the SAFE MLO test, and background checks; renewals require continuing education.

detail.description: Credit analysts examine borrower financials — statements, cash flow, collateral, and ratios — to recommend approvals; the analytical ladder toward commercial lending.
detail.why: Credit analysis is banking's analyst track: strong pay, clear progression, and skills that transfer everywhere in finance.
learn: Learn the 5 Cs applied to real files
Practice spreading financial statements
Calculate key ratios: DSCR, debt-to-income, current ratio
Write one-page credit memos with recommendations

detail.description: Mortgage operations: processing files, coordinating appraisals/title, condition gathering, and regulatory disclosures — the engine room of residential lending.
detail.why: Processing is a licensed-adjacent career with strong remote-work presence and a direct view of the loan officer path.
learn: Learn the loan file milestone flow
Practice condition-gathering checklists
Understand disclosures (Loan Estimate concepts)
Track a mock file from application to clear-to-close

detail.description: Commercial bankers underwrite businesses: working capital lines, equipment loans, CRE — relationships measured in years and memos measured in analysis.
detail.why: Commercial lending is the prestige lane of branch-to-commercial progression, pairing relationship skill with credit rigor.
learn: Learn business entity basics and business credit
Study commercial loan structures (lines, term, CRE)
Practice a mock borrower meeting
Read one commercial credit memo with an analyst

detail.description: Branch wealth roles refer and support investment and retirement relationships; the dedicated track (financial advisor) adds securities licensing — see the Personal Financial Advisor occupation.
detail.why: Wealth is banking's premium service line — bankers who master referrals here open the advisor door.
learn: Learn basic investment products and retirement accounts
Practice warm referral conversations to advisors
Note the securities licensing step (SIE-style) for advisors
Compare bank wealth vs independent RIA careers

detail.description: Compliance and BSA/AML analysts monitor transactions, file reports (SARs), and keep the bank out of trouble — detail-driven roles with strong demand and certification ladders.
detail.why: Regulatory demand makes compliance one of banking's most stable growth tracks — ideal for meticulous investigators.
learn: Learn BSA/AML fundamentals and SAR purpose
Practice transaction-monitoring case reviews
Explore certifications (CAMAS-style) and postings
Follow FinCEN guidance headlines

detail.description: Branch managers own a P&L: sales goals, staffing, coaching, audit readiness, and community presence — the classic destination of the branch ladder.
detail.why: Branch management is general management with real numbers — and the launchpad for market/region leadership.
learn: Learn branch scorecards: deposits, loans, referrals, audits
Practice coaching conversations with tellers
Build a community business-development plan
Shadow a branch manager's full week

detail.description: The credit track grows: analyst → portfolio manager → senior underwriter → credit officer, owning growing loan books and approval authority.
detail.why: Credit authority is banking's senior analytical currency — built file by file over years.
learn: Take on larger, more complex credit files progressively
Learn portfolio-level risk views (concentration, migration)
Present credit opinions in committee
Build a reputation for balanced, defensible calls

resources.title: BLS OOH — Business and Financial occupations

detail.description: Fintech lenders and payment companies hire bank-trained people for operations, credit, and compliance — remote-friendly and faster-paced than traditional banks.
detail.why: Bank experience plus tech comfort is a portable combination — a real option, not a betrayal of the branch.
learn: Follow fintech lenders hiring in your region
Map your banking skills to startup roles
Learn one digital-lending platform's concepts
Weigh equity/risk trade-offs honestly

resources.title: BLS OOH — Business and Financial occupations

detail.description: Branch ladder: teller → banker → assistant manager → branch manager → market leader. Lending ladder: processor → LO → senior LO → lending manager. Credit ladder: analyst → portfolio manager → credit officer.
detail.why: Banking ladders are formal and internally documented — pick your track early and collect the checkpoints deliberately.
learn: Map your bank's internal job families
Ask HR about development programs
Find a sponsor who advocates for promotions
Review your track annually

detail.description: The American Bankers Association and similar bodies offer certificates and diplomas (e.g., ABA Branch Manager Certificate) that banks frequently fund for employees.
detail.why: Structured certificates signal seriousness and often satisfy internal promotion requirements — ask about reimbursement first.
learn: Browse ABA certificate options for your role
Check your bank's tuition-assistance policy
Complete one certificate aligned to your next rung
Log completed training in your HR file

detail.description: Banking sales carry fiduciary-adjacent duties: suitable products, transparent fees, no pushing overdraft or credit a customer can't carry — regulators and communities remember.
detail.why: The industry's worst scandals came from sales-pressure culture. A banker known for honesty keeps customers, regulators, and options.
learn: Learn your bank's sales-practice rules
Practice declining unsuitable products kindly
Document needs behind every recommendation
Escalate pressure you can't manage

detail.description: Entry is via teller/banker postings and internship programs; interviews test accuracy, integrity scenarios, and customer empathy more than finance trivia.
detail.why: A prepared candidate with clean math, integrity answers, and genuine curiosity stands out immediately.
learn: Practice a cash-handling accuracy story
Prepare integrity scenario answers
Learn the bank's products before interviewing
Apply broadly — every bank branches locally

detail.description: Banking rewards continuous learning: products change, regulations update, and markets move — reading one industry item daily compounds into seniority.
detail.why: Senior bankers are the ones who understood the 'why' behind every rule and product — curiosity is the compounding asset.
learn: Follow your central bank's rate communications
Read one banking-industry piece daily
Take one new-product training per quarter
Teach what you learn to newer colleagues
